hero.title: Your AI Safety career starts here.
hero.body: AI Safety expertise has never been more important than today. SAIN provides the community, courses and resources to help students and professionals join the AI Safety field. We provide a clear path through education, community and practical projects, then connect strong contributors to the organisations, programmes and roles where they can take the next step.

meta.title: About
meta.description: Stichting Safe AI Netherlands develops the talent the Netherlands needs to address the risks of transformative AI. The talent pipeline, the foundation documents, and the people who run it.

mission: Develop the talent the Netherlands needs.
Address the risks of transformative AI.
Make a first real contribution possible.
hero.body: That is the mission of Stichting Safe AI Netherlands. Transformative AI could reshape the economy, science, and society on the scale of a major historical revolution; whether that goes well is not decided yet. We are a national talent pipeline: local chapters on shared infrastructure, from first contact through courses and the Project Hub, with a handoff into the wider field. This page shows that path, what we have written down, and the people who run it.

path.heading: The Netherlands has the talent. It lacked the path.
paragraphs: On the current trajectory, AI systems may soon do most economically and strategically important cognitive work, including AI research itself. The critical question is not only what AI will become, but whether enough people are ready to shape what happens next. Right now, far too few are working on that problem.

Nobody can name the exact timeline, and we will not pretend to. Readiness is not something the Netherlands has by default. It is something people build, while European institutions are staffing their AI safety functions in the next few years.

The Netherlands has world-class universities, ASML at the centre of the global semiconductor supply chain, proximity to Brussels, and emerging AI safety groups. What it lacked was a unified civil-society voice and a clear path from interest to capability to meaningful contribution. SAIN was created to close that gap. We develop the people; the field puts them to work.

pipeline.heading: Anyone can start. The path narrows as you grow.
paragraphs: The Funnel Diagram is the whole organisation. The wide end is a free course anyone can join, no technical background required. The narrow end is full-time work on AI safety, in policy, research, industry or civil society. Between them sit the community, the Project Hub, and fellowships. Progress through it is visible, to us and to the person making it, and SAIN’s job is to make each next step reachable, so that every step someone takes compounds into a more effective mission.

We are open about where our effort goes. SAIN builds the wide end: getting people in, teaching foundations, and scaffolding a first real contribution such as a supervised research project. At the narrow end we mainly connect and refer, with introductions and referral letters.

We designed the pipeline with many good endings. Someone who takes one course and returns to law, medicine or public administration carries that knowledge into their profession, and a society fluent in AI risk is an outcome we actively want.
pipeline.record: So far the pipeline has produced more than 100 course graduates across nine-plus cohorts, currently around 60 a year, and peer-reviewed research at NeurIPS and ICLR. The aim for mid-2027 is 250 or more graduates a year, reached by running the same standardised course in more cities.

documents.heading: The rules we hold ourselves to are public.
documents.body: SAIN is a Dutch foundation, a stichting, the standard nonprofit legal form. The foundation holds the brand, the legal entity and the finances, so a local chapter never has to build those from scratch; chapters run their own courses, events and communities. Every programme is free. Three documents define how the whole thing works, and anyone can read them.

work.heading: Six teams, three to ten hours a week
work.body: Amsterdam, Utrecht and Groningen each run the same teams. Leads carry a team and report to the chapter’s director; team members carry a slice of it. Most roles are three to five hours a week, leads six to ten.

education.name: Education
education.description: Run course cohorts and discussion groups. Facilitate weekly sessions, support participants, and keep quality high across iterations.

events.name: Events
events.description: Plan and deliver the chapter's calendar. Hackathons, expert talks, socials, and the logistics behind them.

communications.name: Communications
communications.description: Writing, design, photography, video and the website. Make the chapter's work visible and on-brand.

community.name: Community
community.description: Welcome new members, be the first point of contact, and help people find their way into deeper involvement.

outreach.name: Outreach
outreach.description: Be SAIN's face on campus. Tabling, flyers, and inviting students to upcoming events.

research.name: Research operations
research.description: Keep the Project Hub running day to day. Onboard researchers and supervisors, track projects, and unblock problems.

work.paidNote: SAIN also hires a small number of paid national staff when a role needs it. Those roles are listed with the open positions.

returns.heading: You leave with work you can point to
returns.body: Volunteer roles at SAIN carry real ownership early. Leads report straight to chapter directors, and team members run cohorts, events and channels that actually happen. You work alongside people across Utrecht, Groningen and Amsterdam who are moving into the field themselves, and many of the introductions that matter later start here.

courses.heading: Two free courses run in Amsterdam
courses.note: The courses are independently run by SAIN Amsterdam and are not affiliated with UvA or VU. The certificate of completion is awarded by SAIN Amsterdam, not BlueDot Impact.
technical: Curious where your technical skills could make the biggest difference for AI safety?

SAIN Amsterdam facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Technical AI Safety</course> course for people who want to help close the gap between how fast AI capabilities are advancing and how well we can make them safe. Over six weeks, you’ll diagnose why building safe AI is so technically hard, evaluate current safety techniques (what works, what doesn’t, and where the gaps are), and map how defences might break by building your own “kill chain”. You’ll leave with a fundable action plan for where your skills can make the biggest difference. SAIN Amsterdam supports ambitious students in finding their next steps in an AI safety career.
Technical understanding is ideal, but not a prerequisite. This is a foundational course, covering the foundations of technical AI safety.
governance: What would it take to govern technology that is advancing faster than the rules meant to guide it?

SAIN Amsterdam facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Frontier AI Governance</course> course, which helps you build the judgment to shape how frontier AI is governed. Over six weeks, you’ll assess the evidence, compare competing strategies, and test your ideas through practical exercises and group discussion, leaving with a concrete plan for how you can contribute. Because the course leans heavily on US and China perspectives, our facilitators are encouraged to also bring in European and Dutch materials. Whatever your background, Safe AI Netherlands is here to help you take your next step toward a career in AI safety.
No governance background needed. This is a foundational course that builds up the core ideas of AI governance step by step.

fundamentals.summary: AI Safety Fundamentals has run three times in Utrecht, reaching more than 100 participants: BSc and MSc students, researchers, engineers, and public-sector staff. Four weeks, one hour of reading and a one-hour lecture a week, at Utrecht University in the city centre. In week four you choose a technical path, a governance path, or both. You get a certificate for attending all sessions; no previous background is needed.

sessions.title: Introduction
sessions.detail: High-level overview of AI safety, why it matters now, capabilities and diffusion, types of risks, and solution strategies, technical and governance.

sessions.title: Types of risks and incidents
sessions.detail: Social harms, frontier risks, misuse, loss of control; real-world cases and how research lags behind deployment.

sessions.title: Why AI safety is difficult
sessions.detail: Industry incentives, funding gaps, expert disagreement, slow regulation against fast labs, geopolitical race dynamics.

sessions.title: Path specialisation
sessions.detail: The fourth week splits in two. Take one path, or both.

paths.title: Technical AI safety
paths.detail: Jailbreaking, the scalable oversight problem, RLHF and reward signals.

paths.title: Governance
paths.detail: Overview of the EU AI Act, accountability in AI systems, international actors in AI safety.

technical.summary: Technical AI Safety is a four-week, in-person course at SAIN Utrecht for people who can program and know the basics of AI. Knowing how transformers work is recommended. Each week covers one area of the field: the first two weeks focus on how AI safety evaluators test models, week three looks at safety in robots and other physical systems, and week four covers securing AI agents. The weekly assignments use material from ARENA, an established AI safety training programme, and especially strong solutions are sent to ARENA for review and may be added to their repository. A workshop every Saturday from 13:00 to 15:00 helps you complete them. After the course, we launch a research challenge where our mentors help you develop your own ideas. Each week has about one hour of reading, one to three hours of assignments and a 1.5-hour lecture.

sessions.title: Introduction to AI safety evaluations
sessions.detail: What evaluations are and why we need them, capability versus alignment evaluations, and how to design one: threat models, datasets and scoring.

sessions.title: Implementing and evaluating AI safety evaluations
sessions.detail: Running evaluations in practice with tools, understanding the common problems that make results unreliable, and how results are communicated to policymakers.

sessions.title: Embodied AI safety
sessions.detail: The safety risks of robots and other physical AI systems, safety filters, using vision-language models to spot unsafe actions, and measuring uncertainty.

sessions.title: Securing AI agents
sessions.detail: How agents are attacked through prompt injection and their tools, why model-level defences fail, secure design and AI Control, and how AI can also act as a defender.

governance.summary: AI Governance is a new four-week course at SAIN Utrecht, open to everyone, with no previous background needed. Most AI governance courses focus on the US and China. In this course, we also look at their visions and ambitions and at where middle powers like the EU fit in. We also dedicate an entire lecture to how Europe and the Netherlands are regulating AI. Throughout the course, we read and discuss primary sources, such as government strategies, laws, and documents from AI labs, giving you the tools to follow developments in AI regulation and geopolitics independently. Each week has about one to two hours of reading and a 1.5-hour lecture.

sessions.title: Introduction to AI governance and AI safety
sessions.detail: What AI governance is, how it differs from technical safety, why it matters now, and the main risks: misuse, loss of control, and concentration of power.

sessions.title: AI geopolitics
sessions.detail: The key actors (governments, labs, safety organisations, the UN), US and Chinese visions and ambitions, and where middle powers fit.

sessions.title: The tools of the policymaker
sessions.detail: Analysis of past incidents like the Hugging Face case, system cards, and future scenarios.

sessions.title: Governance in Europe and the Netherlands
sessions.detail: The EU AI Act and its gaps, the EU AI Office and the GPAI Code of Practice, the Dutch AI landscape.

courses.discussionGroups: Between cohorts, two discussion groups keep meeting: one on technical AI safety, currently a mechanistic interpretability reading group, and one on AI governance and policy.
courses.research: The chapter is building a research track: red-teaming language models, safety evaluation, interpretability, and agent behaviour. The Project Hub launches in October 2026.

utrecht.teamBody: SAIN Utrecht is directed by Riccardo Campanella. The team is growing across four areas: education, events, communication, and research. The chapter's work is funded by BERI, with mentorship from Pathfinder.

evidence.heading: This already happened in Utrecht
evidence.body: Over the past year the chapter ran the Win4AISafety open research summer challenge, a full technical course with a closing dinner, discussion groups including a Europe 2031 scenario session, and research talks, including an Anthropic researcher speaking to more than 60 people.
evidence.contributed: Members of SAIN Utrecht contributed to this research.

courses.heading: Join one of our free courses!
courses.note: The courses are independently run by SAIN Groningen and are not affiliated with the University of Groningen (RUG). The certificate of completion is awarded by SAIN Groningen, not BlueDot Impact. Questions: {email}.
technical: Curious to learn about the technical approaches to AI safety?

SAIN Groningen facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Technical AI Safety</course> course for people who want to learn about the open problems in technical AI safety and the techniques to address them. It takes six weeks, with about three hours of reading and a two-hour discussion session each week. The discussion sessions are guided by a facilitator, creating the perfect space to both discuss the material and connect with others who are eager to work on AI safety too.
governance: Curious to learn about the governance challenges around AI safety?

SAIN Groningen facilitates the <bluedot>BlueDot Impact</bluedot> <course>Frontier AI Governance</course> course, which helps you build the judgment to shape how frontier AI is governed. Since the BlueDot course mainly covers the US and China dynamic, we have extended the curriculum with hand-picked materials on tackling AI safety from the EU’s perspective. The course takes six weeks, with about three hours of reading and a two-hour discussion session each week. The discussion sessions are guided by a facilitator, creating the perfect space to both discuss the materials in detail and connect with others who are eager to work on AI safety too.
courses.discussionGroups: Two discussion groups meet through the year, each with at least one experienced mentor: technical AI alignment (scalable oversight, evaluation and red-teaming, preference learning, robustness, deployment risks) and AI governance and privacy (policies, regulations, accountability, transparency and fairness).

groningen.teamBody: SAIN Groningen is directed by Tarteel Mohamed, with work organised across four teams: education, events, communications, and research operations; a structure other chapters are adopting as they spin up. The chapter grew out of the AI Safety Initiative Groningen (AISIG), running since 2023.

evidence.heading: 30 events and counting
evidence.body: Since October 2023 the chapter has run 30 events: hackathons, course graduations, research talks, pub quizzes, and socials; first as AISIG and, since 30 April 2026, as SAIN Groningen. Members' research has been published at NeurIPS and ICLR workshops.

meta.title: Start a chapter in Eindhoven, Delft or The Hague
meta.description: SAIN is starting chapters in Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague. Each city gets a paid, part-time starting team of four: a Chapter Director and leads for education, events and communications.

hero.heading: Start SAIN in Eindhoven, Delft or The Hague.
hero.body: SAIN has chapters in Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht. This winter we are starting three more: Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague. Each city gets a starting team of four people: a Chapter Director, an Education Lead, an Events Lead and a Communications Lead. All four roles are paid and part-time.
hero.deadline: Soft deadline {deadline}. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority to early applicants.

building.heading: You would be building a chapter, not joining one.
building.body: You would be the person building a SAIN chapter in your city, and you will be in charge of setting up everything. However, you’ll have support: a funded national organisation behind you, and a network of advisors, researchers and partner organisations who want nothing more than your chapter to succeed.

cities.heading: Three cities with the most potential.
cities.body: We have identified these three cities as the highest-potential ones for us to expand to. Here is, very briefly, why we think so.
cities.inTouch: We are already in touch with people working on AI safety in these cities. Where people have already been running things, we can build on top of that and be much more ambitious. Already running something there and not heard from us yet? <link>Please get in touch</link>, so we can work together instead of duplicating efforts.

incubation.heading: Six months from starting team to SAIN chapter.
paragraphs: New chapters start as incubating chapters. From mid-December 2026 to June 2027, the starting team will develop the chapter towards a few concrete milestones. Importantly, although this phase is part of the incubation, internally we’ll treat you as a SAIN chapter from the start.

We’re ambitious about this. In some of these cities, people already run AI safety courses, and we want to build on that and go much further: courses with dozens of participants, events that bring hundreds of new people into AI safety, a community of hundreds in every city, and people moving on into real projects.

The exact milestones for June 2027 we’ll set together with you in your first weeks; how you get there is up to you. We’ll work together to make sure you reach your fullest potential. In June 2027 we will do a final review of how things have gone. Chapters that get there become official SAIN chapters, and the director and lead roles stay paid part-time positions.

community.heading: This is what you would be starting.
community.body: Discussion groups, hackathons, talks, and the evenings after. In Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht, people meet friends and collaborators at SAIN, and often find their next step in AI safety. Apply now, and a year from now your city has a community like this, built by you.

offer.heading: You won’t be doing it alone.
offer.body: Everything the three existing chapters learned the hard way is written down, set up, and yours from day one.

roles.heading: Four roles in every city.
roles.body: Every starting team has the same four roles. Open one for the full description. You can apply for more than one, and the form asks which city you are based in.

apply.heading: One form, and a decision by mid-December.
apply.body: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority to early applicants. The soft deadline is {deadline}.
apply.hearBackHeading: Everyone who applies hears back from us.
apply.hearBackBody: If you are not in the starting team, you are still the start of the chapter’s community! We will send you what you need to join SAIN’s online community, so you are among the first to hear about new activities and opportunities in your city.
apply.strongTeamHeading: We only start a chapter when the team is strong enough.
apply.strongTeamBody: If we do not have strong enough applications to start the incubation in a particular city, we will open a second round later on.
apply.aboutBody: Safe AI Netherlands (SAIN) is a Dutch non-profit developing the talent the Netherlands needs to address the risks of transformative AI. We build the national AI safety talent pipeline to get people from first contact to first real contribution. Then we connect them to the institutions and organisations that need them.
apply.visas: We do not sponsor visas. If you are in the Netherlands on a student residence permit, you can still apply.

close.heading: Three new chapters. Twelve people to start them.
close.body: Apply by {deadline}. We read applications every week, so applying early means hearing back early.

meta.title: Project hub
meta.description: The SAIN Project Hub matches you with an experienced supervisor, arranges compute, and takes a project from open question to published finding. Voluntary, remote-friendly, and open for applications at any time.

hero.heading: Make a first real contribution to AI Safety
hero.body: The SAIN Project Hub matches you with an experienced supervisor, arranges compute, and takes a project from open question to published finding. It is voluntary, remote-friendly, and open for applications at any time.
hero.illustrationLabel: A scatter of observations on a plot. Two researchers, one seated and one standing and pointing, fit a single line through it; the fitted line rises clear of the scatter in orange and runs onto a pinned printed page, whose figure repeats the same line.

projects.heading: Find a project, then join it
projects.body: Every project SAIN supervisors have on offer, kept up to date by the projects team. One application form covers all of them: name up to three projects in it, and the projects team will introduce you to the supervisors within a working week. A VU or UvA thesis counts towards a degree there, so it is for that university’s students; every other project is open to anyone with the right background.

eligibility.heading: You do not need a university post to do this work
eligibility.offer: SAIN’s offer is one line: bring your expertise to AI Safety, and the community, supervision, and support are here to take it further. The rest of this page is the mechanism behind that line: how a project is chosen, what support looks like week to week, and where the work ends up.
eligibility.openTo: The hub is open to anyone with sufficient background:
who: Students at Bachelor, Master, or PhD level
Researchers, and people working in industry
eligibility.remote: Remote participation works. Applications are rolling, so you can apply whenever you are ready, and for supervised projects you hear back within a working week.
eligibility.notAJob: One thing the hub is not: a job. SAIN does not pay stipends or salaries; participation is voluntary and educational. What SAIN does provide is supervision, compute, coordination, and, within reason, help with conference travel.

process.heading: From open question to published finding
process.body: Every project in the hub moves through the same three steps. The handbook spells each one out in full; this is the shape of it.
process.label: The three steps of a project

choose.title: Choose a project
choose.intro: There are three ways in, and all three are normal.

routes.body: Every project a SAIN supervisor has offered is listed at the top of this page. Find one that fits your background and register your interest; the projects team introduces you to the supervisor.
Some projects run without formal supervision. One person leads, usually whoever designed the project, and SAIN connects collaborators and supports the work.
Write a short proposal: the question, why it matters, how you would test it, and what you need. SAIN's Project Team reviews it, and can help you shape it if it is not fully formed yet.

choose.criteria: Not every valuable contribution is a research paper: the work can be technical, governance, policy, or conceptual. When choosing projects, the team looks at three things: relevance to the Netherlands and Europe, relevance to transformative AI, and whether it can succeed on a small budget. If you are unsure whether a topic counts as AI Safety, the default answer is yes, provided you can articulate a plausible pathway from the work to reducing risk from transformative AI.

support.title: Work with support
paragraphs: Fill in the application form and, for supervised projects, you hear back within a working week. If there is a fit, a supervisor is formally assigned and the project gets its own channel in the community.

Supervision is a working relationship, not a lecture. You drive the day-to-day work; your supervisor helps scope the project realistically, reviews experiments and drafts, and steps in when a direction stops being productive. Meetings run weekly or biweekly, and you agree your commitment per project up front, whether that is five to ten hours a week alongside a degree or something closer to full time.

Supervisors come from universities, industry, and government. In academia they are usually at PhD level or more senior; outside it, they have several years of senior experience in a relevant role. Compute is arranged per project at the start, and computationally inexpensive projects are encouraged. Remote participation works throughout.

publish.title: Publish your findings
paragraphs: A project is complete when its main question is adequately answered, including when the answer is negative, and the result is published in a presentable form: a paper, a policy brief, an evaluation or open-source tool, or a blog post on SAIN’s Substack or LessWrong. You get feedback on drafts, and SAIN may help with conference travel within reason.
That is not hypothetical. Work from this community has been accepted at workshops at NeurIPS and ICLR, which is where most first contributions in this field land.
publish.allPublicationsLabel: All publications from the SAIN community

supervisors.heading: The people you would work with
supervisors.body: Every supervisor keeps a public agenda of the projects they would like to supervise. Read it before you apply: the strongest expressions of interest respond to a question a supervisor has already posed.
supervisors.superviseBody: If you have substantial experience in a relevant field, usually PhD level or above in academia or several years in a senior role in industry or policy, and the work above looks like something you could guide, more supervisors means more projects. You do not need to be an AI Safety expert already. Supervision is remote-friendly, meetings run at a cadence you agree per project, and the Project Team handles the coordination around you. Fill in the supervisor form and we will follow up with next steps.

close.heading: Apply whenever you are ready
close.body: Applications are rolling, and for supervised projects you hear back within a working week. Fill in the application form, or email the projects team if you are not sure where you fit and we will help route you.
close.handbookNote: The full process, expectations, and norms are written down. <link>Read the Project Hub handbook</link>
